FINDING, the real one this proof is for: git worktree add -b <branch> <dir> HEAD only checks out COMMITTED history. This repo's main tree stays uncommitted by design (CLAUDE.md: production is static, the main tree is never committed by an agent) - so proof-1's worktree, checked out at HEAD (3e9536d4), does NOT contain today's days-view feature at all (0 matches for days_view/day_row/day_working vs 8 in the main tree's own uncommitted page.js). A worktree here starts from whatever was last committed, which on this repo can be hours or days behind what is actually on screen. Decision: copy today's three uncommitted v/3/ files (page.js, v3.css, readme.md) into the worktree first and commit them there as a named baseline commit, so the worktree's branch actually contains the feature I am about to patch - then make the real fix as its own separate commit, so deliverable 4's cherry-pick carries only the fix, not a second copy of the whole days-view feature. Alternative rejected: patch the stale pre-days-view page.js in the worktree - it has no days_view() to patch at all, so the deliverable as asked would be impossible without this step.

Days-view follow-up fixed in the worktree (public/framework/ai/v/3/page.js): day_row's summary now renders b(slug) then a span with the sentence, imported b from /app.js; day_working switched from a.c(...).href(...) to div.c(...) - no href, so a working row can no longer be clicked. Proven headless with a Playwright probe against the worktree's own server on 53765 at 1280 and 400 (shots saved to this task's shots/ in the MAIN tree, not the worktree): status 200 both widths, first_summary_has_bold true, first_summary_html shows slug - sentence, working_is_link false against a synthetic today-day.jsonl I added and removed again purely to exercise that path (no real working task existed in the worktree's stale, pre-today checkout). decision.msg: Bringing the worktree's fix commit (1518d075) home: git cherry-pick -n refused outright - 'Your local changes... would be overwritten by merge' - because the main tree's page.js already carries the WHOLE days-view feature as an uncommitted change, so git's 3-way merge sees local modifications relative to HEAD even though the file's actual bytes match the worktree's pre-fix commit (dd3d5909) exactly (diffed and confirmed identical first). Used git diff dd3d5909 1518d075 -- page.js > patch, then git apply patch in the main tree instead - same effect (the fix's own lines land on disk, nothing committed), no cherry-pick needed once the base already matches on disk. This only worked because I had verified byte-parity first; on a repo where the main tree is never committed, cherry-pick is the wrong tool whenever the file already has uncommitted local changes - a plain patch apply against a known-identical base is the real move. node --check passed on the patched file.

DELIVERABLE 2, the proxy gap: Servex scans C:/Code to depth 2 (Servex.js scan()) - for C:/Code/lew42/worktrees/proof-1 to be found, some directory at depth 1 under C:/Code/lew42 would need its OWN package.json, but worktrees/ itself has none (it is a container of worktrees, each with a package.json one level deeper than the scan reaches). Confirmed live: GET /api/projects on the running Servex (127.0.0.1:8090) lists monorepo and ten others but nothing named proof-1. PortRegistry.pin(name, port) is the exact call that would fix this (Servex.js already uses it once, for its own dashboard name) and ReverseProxy holds a LIVE reference to that same ports object (Servex.js: 'ports: this.ports.ports') - so a pinned name would route immediately with no restart, IF something could call pin() from outside the running process. Nothing on the /mcp door does: list_servers/append_log/start_server et al never touch the port map, and Servex/ is outside this task's fence, so I cannot add the one route (POST /api/register {name, port} calling this.ports.pin then updating this.proxy.ports) myself. Proved instead: curl -H 'Host: proof-1.localhost' http://127.0.0.1:8080/framework/ -> 404 (no route, as expected); curl http://127.0.0.1:53765/framework/ (the worktree's own port, direct) -> 200; headless-loaded the same direct url, zero console errors. What Servex needs, in one line: a route (or an MCP tool) that calls PortRegistry.pin(name, port) and is called once by worktree-up.mjs after it boots the worktree's server.
